name: express-send-status-wsfed
behavioral_change: express 5.0.0 removed the special interpretation of a numeric first argument to `res.send` and the two-argument form `res.send(status, body)`. In v_old, `res.send(400, 'postUrl is required')` sent status 400 with that text; in v_new the first argument is serialized as the response body by `res.json`, the second is ignored, and the response silently becomes status 200 with body `400`.
downstream_effect: In the downstream project (wsfed), requests that should be rejected are answered as successes; the two failing tests report only `expected 200 to equal 400` with no stack frames, file names or line numbers. The edit site is `lib/wsfed.js:149` inside an anonymous middleware closure, reachable only by tracing through `test/fixture/server.js`.
reference_fix: The reference fix edits only `lib/wsfed.js`, changing `res.send(400, 'postUrl is required')` at line 149 to `res.status(400).send('postUrl is required')` and `res.send(401)` at line 89 to `res.sendStatus(401)`.
documented_in: The express 5 migration guide (https://expressjs.com/en/guide/migrating-5.html), section Removed, has entries for `res.send(status)` and `res.send(body, status)`, each with a How to update example showing `res.sendStatus(200)` and `res.status(200).send({ name: 'Ruben' })`. Tier 1: the documentation shows the new code form.
failing_tests: test/wsfed.tests.js :: wsfed > when using an invalid callback url > should return error
test/wsfed.custom_form.tests.js :: wsfed > when using an invalid callback url > should return error
